label: F-14B(U) Tomcat (DCS DTC)
pathSyntax: Dot-separated keys of the .dtc "data" object. "[]" = any array index, "{}" = any object key, each as its own segment (e.g. NAV.[].waypoints.[].lat, CMDS.CMDSProgramSettings.{}.Priority). An array/object is user-extensible only when its section has a "template"; "maxItems"/"fixedLength" bound it ("fixedLength" on an object = number of keys, all required). "{index}" in itemLabel is 1-based. "itemLabels" (array) names fixed array slots in order; "keyLabels" names object keys. A field with "optional": true is absent from a fresh cartridge (Lua nil) and may stay absent. Sections marked hidden cover a whole derived/internal subtree. "display" = {unit, factor, decimals}: shown value = stored value * factor. For kind string, "maxLength"/"pattern" constrain the text.
source: DCS 2.9.30.28738 CoreMods/aircraft/F14/DTC/F-14BU_DTC.lua (+ Heatblur F-14B(U) manual: MDL, ALE-47, GGW, FTI); see native-F-14BU.md and EXPORT-NOTES.md

sections.label: F-14B(U) Tomcat cartridge (MDL / DTM)
sections.help: Root of data. Four ME tabs: Navigation (12 MDL flight plans), CMDS (AN/ALE-47 programmer), JDAM (GBU-31 pre-planned missions) and TIS (Tactical Imaging Set). No terrain key and no upload flags: everything in the file is loaded. Only unit type F-14BU uses this cartridge (F-14B/F-14A get a DTC tab but no F-14 cartridge).

sections.label: Navigation: MDL flight plans 1-12
sections.help: Exactly 12 flight plans as a JSON array (an object keyed "1".."12" is silently ignored: every plan loads empty). Plan 1 is always the Mission Editor route ("1: ME Route"): its waypoints come from the mission and cannot be edited in the DTC, but its plot lines and additional points can. Plans 2-12 are planned here; a plan must have a name to be selectable on the CDNU MDL FPLN page. Each plan holds at most 50 points in total: waypoints + all plot-line points + additional points. The exporter writes the planned route into plan 2 (the second array element, NAV[1] in 0-based JSON) and leaves plan 1 waypoints empty.

sections.label: Flight plan
sections.help: One MDL flight plan: name, route-as-line flag, waypoints (route, in order), up to 4 plot lines and free-standing additional points.

sections.label: Flight-plan waypoints
sections.help: Route waypoints in flight order. Generated by the exporter: plan 2 (NAV[1]) = the planned route; plans 3-12 = further planner routes if the planner has them, else []; plan 1 must stay [] (the ME route; the DTC UI refuses waypoint edits on plan 1 and what the jet does with plan-1 waypoints from a file is untested). Counts toward the 50-point plan limit together with plot-line points and additional points; setData truncates to 50.

sections.label: Plot lines
sections.help: Up to 4 PTID plot lines (3 when route_as_line is on; setData truncates to 4). Plot-line points are appended after the flight-plan waypoints in the 50-point plan. Manual: up to 9 points per line and at most 20 plot-line points in total per plan (NAV_MAX_TOTAL_REFS, not enforced by the ME: enforce it yourself). Editable on every plan including plan 1. The exporter may also fill them from planner map drawings (FEBA, boundaries).

sections.label: Line points
sections.help: Points of the line in order: max 9 (8 when closed). setData truncates to 9.

sections.label: Additional points
sections.help: Free-standing flight-plan waypoints not tied to the route or a plot line (LANTIRN targets, airfields, bullseye, other references). They count toward the 50-point plan limit. Editable on every plan including plan 1. The exporter may fill them from planner map markers.

sections.label: CMDS: AN/ALE-47 programmer
sections.help: Countermeasure bingo, the 8 dispense programs, the automatic program per threat category and per-threat overrides. Must be present: a cartridge without CMDS crashes the ME DTC editor (init_CMDS indexes CMDSProgramSettings.PROG_1). Merged field by field over the defaults on import. Manual: program 8 = pilot (DLC switch), 5/6 = RIO hand-hold up/down, 7 = outboard (Jester default), 1-4 = manual/semi/auto via the inboard switch.

sections.label: Countermeasure bingo
sections.help: When a count reaches its bingo the ALE-47 panel shows LoXX.

sections.label: Dispense programs 1-8
sections.help: Programs PROG_1..PROG_8, each with a priority and four dispenser sub-programs (Chaff, Flare, Other1, Other2). Burst = cartridges per burst and the time between them; salvo = number of bursts and the time between bursts. Keep all 8 keys.

sections.label: Chaff sub-program
sections.help: Chaff dispensing for this program. All zero = this dispenser is not used.

sections.label: Flare sub-program
sections.help: Flare dispensing for this program. All zero = this dispenser is not used.

sections.label: Other 1 sub-program
sections.help: Other 1 dispensing for this program. All zero = this dispenser is not used.

sections.label: Other 2 sub-program
sections.help: Other 2 dispensing for this program. All zero = this dispenser is not used.

sections.label: Automatic program per threat category
sections.help: The program the ALE-47 selects (SEMI) or fires (AUTO) when the RWR reports a threat of that category at or above the threshold. Defaults: SAM 5/Launch, AAA 2/Track, Aircraft 4/Launch, Naval 5/Launch, Unknown 4/Launch.

sections.label: Per-threat overrides
sections.help: Object keyed by canonical DCS unit type (the 71 types the ME picker offers, see keyOptions/keyLabels: "display [category] (RWR symbol)"). Overrides the category program for that emitter. Empty = [] (JSON.lua writes an empty table as []). Replaced wholesale on import; entries without Program are dropped. setData accepts any string key.

sections.label: JDAM: GBU-31 pre-planned missions
sections.help: Up to 8 pre-planned missions (PP1..PP8) per JDAM station 3, 4, 5, 6: target, attack heading, release conditions and launch point. The jet draws the PPLAR and launch-point cues from them; LAR data cannot be changed in flight. After loading the cartridge, UPDATE the JDAMs on the JMSN page. Recommended release order 4-5-3-6.

sections.label: Stations
sections.help: Exactly 4 entries in the order STA 3, STA 4, STA 5, STA 6. Must be a JSON array (setData walks 1..4 numerically).

sections.label: Pre-planned missions
sections.help: Exactly 8 entries PP1..PP8, JSON array. Missing slots are recreated with defaults; each target is merged field by field over the defaults and its LAR scalars are recomputed on import.

sections.label: TIS: Tactical Imaging Set
sections.help: Ownship callsign and send-to directory for the Fast Tactical Imaging Set. Must be present with send_to_callsigns: a cartridge without TIS crashes the ME DTC editor (ipairs over nil); 9 of 101 ED-shipped F-14BU cartridges have this bug.

sections.label: Send-to callsigns
sections.help: Callsign directory (first entry = SND on the TIS page). Each entry 6 chars, upper case, blank-padded; all-blank entries are dropped on import; the UI rejects duplicates. No count limit in the descriptor.

fields.label: Aircraft type
fields.help: Must be exactly "F-14BU". setData compares data.type; anything else leaves the ME with an empty skeleton (and the next ME save writes that skeleton).

fields.label: Internal cartridge name
fields.help: Cosmetic copy of the cartridge name inside data ("F-14BU DTC" in a fresh cartridge; ED files often hold stale names). DCS indexes cartridges by the outer .dtc "name"; the exporter writes the same string here.

fields.label: Cartridge label
fields.help: The label printed on the cartridge and shown on the CDNU MDL start page (display line 3). Default "DEFAULT". No length cap in the descriptor; keep it short (the CDNU line is narrow, 8-12 characters is safe).

fields.label: Plan name
fields.help: Up to 16 characters (NAV_PLAN_NAME_MAXLEN). Shown on the CDNU FPLN and MDL pages. A plan without a name cannot be selected on the CDNU, so the exporter names plan 2 after the planned route (first 16 chars) when the user left it empty. Plan 1 shows as "1: ME Route" when empty.

fields.label: Draw route as plot line
fields.help: Draws the flight-plan route itself as a plot line on the PTID. It uses one of the 4 line slots, so with this on at most 3 user plot lines are allowed (the UI deletes the 4th).

fields.label: Waypoint label
fields.help: Up to 8 chars (NAV_WP_NAME_MAXLEN). The CDNU shows a 5-char root; optional suffixes set designations: "X" + special point FP/IP/HB/DP/HA/ST (e.g. OCEANXHB), then B = bullseye, D = destination, 1-3 = priority, 4-7 = generic priority, L = LANTIRN (e.g. DALLSXB, LANDXD). Two waypoints with the same special/bullseye suffix make the jet ignore both. Upper-case letters and digits.

fields.label: Latitude
fields.help: Decimal degrees WGS84 (+N). Stored together with x/y; both must describe the same point (the ME writes lat/lon = convertMetersToLatLon(x, y)).

fields.label: Longitude
fields.help: Decimal degrees WGS84 (+E).

fields.label: Map X (north)
fields.help: DCS map metres, x = north (mission x). Computed by the exporter from lat/lon with the theatre projection. The ME map draws the point from x/y.

fields.label: Map Y (east)
fields.help: DCS map metres, y = east (mission y = world z).

fields.label: Waypoint elevation
fields.help: FEET. Ground elevation of the point (the ME sets round(terrain_m * 3.28084)), not the planned flight altitude. UI range 0..60000 step 100.

fields.label: Desired ground speed
fields.help: Desired ground speed in knots, 0 = none. UI range 0..999 step 10. Mutually exclusive with TOT in the UI (speed > 0 disables TOT). Must be a number: a string crashes the waypoint grid ("spd > 0").

fields.label: Time on target
fields.help: Free text, "" = none. No parser in the descriptor and no shipped example, so the format the CDNU expects is unknown; the exporter leaves it "" and uses spd instead. Mutually exclusive with spd in the UI.

fields.label: Closed line
fields.help: Connects the last point back to the first. The closing point uses a slot, so a closed line takes at most 8 points; setData silently clears closed when a closed line has more than 8.

fields.label: Latitude
fields.help: Decimal degrees WGS84 (+N). Write x/y too (exporter: from lat/lon).

fields.label: Longitude
fields.help: Decimal degrees WGS84 (+E).

fields.label: Map X (north)
fields.help: DCS map metres (north). Derived from lat/lon by the exporter.

fields.label: Map Y (east)
fields.help: DCS map metres (east). Derived from lat/lon by the exporter.

fields.label: Point elevation
fields.help: FEET, ground elevation (the ME writes round(terrain_m * 3.28084)).

fields.label: Point label
fields.help: Up to 8 chars, same suffix rules as waypoint labels (e.g. BULLSXB for the bullseye, TGT1XL for a LANTIRN point). Empty shows as AP<n> on the ME map.

fields.label: Latitude
fields.help: Decimal degrees WGS84 (+N). Write x/y too.

fields.label: Longitude
fields.help: Decimal degrees WGS84 (+E).

fields.label: Map X (north)
fields.help: DCS map metres (north). Derived from lat/lon by the exporter.

fields.label: Map Y (east)
fields.help: DCS map metres (east). Derived from lat/lon by the exporter.

fields.label: Point elevation
fields.help: FEET, ground elevation.

fields.label: Chaff bingo
fields.help: Chaff bingo: remaining count that triggers the LoXX bingo cue. 0..99.

fields.label: Flare bingo
fields.help: Flare bingo: remaining count that triggers the LoXX bingo cue. 0..99.

fields.label: Other 1 bingo
fields.help: Other 1 bingo: remaining count that triggers the LoXX bingo cue. 0..99.

fields.label: Other 2 bingo
fields.help: Other 2 bingo: remaining count that triggers the LoXX bingo cue. 0..99.

fields.label: Priority
fields.help: Program priority 0..9: starting a lower-priority program while a higher one runs has no effect; a higher one overrides the running program.

fields.label: Chaff burst quantity
fields.help: Chaff cartridges per burst, 0..99.

fields.label: Chaff burst interval
fields.help: Seconds between chaff cartridges within a burst, 0..10 step 0.01.

fields.label: Chaff salvo quantity
fields.help: Number of chaff bursts in the salvo, 0..99.

fields.label: Chaff salvo interval
fields.help: Seconds between chaff bursts, 0..10 step 0.01.

fields.label: Flare burst quantity
fields.help: Flare cartridges per burst, 0..99.

fields.label: Flare burst interval
fields.help: Seconds between flare cartridges within a burst, 0..10 step 0.01.

fields.label: Flare salvo quantity
fields.help: Number of flare bursts in the salvo, 0..99.

fields.label: Flare salvo interval
fields.help: Seconds between flare bursts, 0..10 step 0.01.

fields.label: Other 1 burst quantity
fields.help: Other 1 cartridges per burst, 0..99.

fields.label: Other 1 burst interval
fields.help: Seconds between other 1 cartridges within a burst, 0..10 step 0.01.

fields.label: Other 1 salvo quantity
fields.help: Number of other 1 bursts in the salvo, 0..99.

fields.label: Other 1 salvo interval
fields.help: Seconds between other 1 bursts, 0..10 step 0.01.

fields.label: Other 2 burst quantity
fields.help: Other 2 cartridges per burst, 0..99.

fields.label: Other 2 burst interval
fields.help: Seconds between other 2 cartridges within a burst, 0..10 step 0.01.

fields.label: Other 2 salvo quantity
fields.help: Number of other 2 bursts in the salvo, 0..99.

fields.label: Other 2 salvo interval
fields.help: Seconds between other 2 bursts, 0..10 step 0.01.

fields.label: Program
fields.help: 0 = NONE (no automatic response; the threshold is then ignored), 1..8 = PROG_1..PROG_8.

fields.label: Threshold
fields.help: RWR state that triggers the program: 1 Search, 2 Track, 3 Launch. ED recommends Launch for most categories (Search fires on every passing scan).

fields.label: Program
fields.help: 1..8 = PROG_1..PROG_8 (NONE is not offered for overrides). Required: an override without Program is dropped.

fields.label: Threshold
fields.help: 1 Search, 2 Track, 3 Launch. Missing = 2 (Track).

fields.label: Active
fields.help: Only active targets are drawn and used. Set true whenever the target has a position.

fields.label: Target name
fields.help: Shown on the PTID JMSN page. No cap in the descriptor; keep it short (about 8 chars).

fields.label: Target latitude
fields.help: Decimal degrees WGS84 (+N). Absent while unset. Write x/y and lat/lon together.

fields.label: Target longitude
fields.help: Decimal degrees WGS84 (+E). Absent while unset.

fields.label: Target map X (north)
fields.help: DCS map metres (north), derived from lat/lon by the exporter. An active target without x/y is not drawn.

fields.label: Target map Y (east)
fields.help: DCS map metres (east), derived from lat/lon by the exporter.

fields.label: Target elevation
fields.help: METRES (unlike NAV, which uses feet). The ME UI shows/edits feet 0..50000 step 100 and stores ft / 3.28084; placing a target stores the terrain height in metres.

fields.label: Attack heading
fields.help: Run-in heading toward the target, 0..359.9 step 0.1. The LAR is drawn behind the target, opposite this heading, in map-grid geometry (grid north, not true north).

fields.label: Impact heading set
fields.help: Enables impact_heading. Informational only: the LAR ignores it.

fields.label: Impact heading
fields.help: Terminal (impact) heading the weapon tries to achieve, 0..359. Used only when has_impact_heading is true. Drawn as the terminal heading cue.

fields.label: Impact angle set
fields.help: Enables impact_angle. Informational only.

fields.label: Impact angle
fields.help: Terminal impact angle 30..85 step 5, default 65. Used only when has_impact_angle is true.

fields.label: Release altitude
fields.help: FEET MSL, 10000..50000 step 500, default 20000. Drives the LAR (lar_* recomputed).

fields.label: Release ground speed
fields.help: Knots ground speed (treated as TAS in still air), 250..750 step 10, default 450. Drives the LAR.

fields.label: Launch point map X
fields.help: Pre-planned launch point, DCS map metres (north). Absent = the ME puts it at the LAR centre the next time it draws the target. Must lie inside the LAR polygon or the ME snaps it to the nearest edge. See derived[].

fields.label: Launch point map Y
fields.help: Launch point, DCS map metres (east). See launch_x.

fields.label: LAR minimum range
fields.help: Cached LAR scalar, derived from drop_alt/drop_spd (derived[]). The ME recomputes it on import; the jet may read it straight from the file, so the exporter must write it.

fields.label: LAR maximum range
fields.help: Cached LAR scalar, derived (derived[]).

fields.label: LAR half angle
fields.help: Cached LAR scalar, derived (derived[]).

fields.label: Use mission callsign
fields.help: true (default): the jet uses the mission unit callsign and ignores own_callsign.

fields.label: Own callsign
fields.help: Exactly 6 characters A-Z, 0-9 or blank, upper case, blank-padded on the right (default 6 blanks). setData sanitises it the same way. Used only when use_mission_callsign is false.

fields.label: Add wingmen to send list
fields.help: true (default): the jet adds the flight members' callsigns to the send-to list.

fields.label: Callsign
fields.help: 6 characters A-Z, 0-9, blank-padded on the right (e.g. "VF103 "). Not all blanks.

derived.formula: x, y = theatreProjection(lat, lon) -> DCS map metres (x north, y east), the same transform the ME uses (convertLatLonToMeters). Applies to every x/y in NAV (waypoints, line points, additional points) and to JDAM x/y.
elev_ft = Math.floor(groundElevation_m(x, y) * 3.28084 + 0.5)  // terrain height, not flight altitude; same for lines.[].points.[].elev and additional_points.[].elev

NAV[1].waypoints (plan 2) = route.points.map(p => ({ name: label(p), x: p.x, y: p.y, lat: p.lat, lon: p.lon, elev: elevFt(p), spd: p.gs_kt ? Math.min(999, Math.round(p.gs_kt / 10) * 10) : 0, tot: "" })); NAV[0].waypoints = []; extra planner routes k = 1.. go to NAV[1 + k] (plans 3..12). Truncate so that waypoints + line points + additional points <= 50 per plan.

label(p) = (p.name || ("WP" + n)).toUpperCase().replace(/[^A-Z0-9]/g, "").slice(0, 5) + suffix, total <= 8 chars. suffix = "" by default; optional "X" + one of FP/IP/HB/DP/HA/ST, then B/D/1-7/L. Never give two points of one plan the same special or bullseye suffix (the jet ignores all of them).
if (plan has waypoints && name === "") name = (route.name || "ROUTE").slice(0, 16)  // unnamed plans cannot be selected on the CDNU
elev_m = groundElevation_m(x, y) (or user feet / 3.28084). Metres, unlike NAV elev.
sanitize(s) = (s ?? "").toUpperCase().replace(/[^A-Z0-9 ]/g, "").slice(0, 6).padEnd(6, " ")  // same for send_to_callsigns.[]; drop results equal to "      "; de-duplicate
